attacks.name: Bite
attacks.text: 5/7/9 damage. On a strong or critical hit against a creature of equal or smaller size, the target falls prone.

lore.narrative: A lean grey scavenger of the burial roads. Jackals follow funerals at the edge of a thrown stone's range, and they have learned which funerals leave food. Every gravedigger knows the ones that work their stretch, and none of them has ever driven one off for good.
lore.ecology: They eat what is left. Offerings, grave goods with fat in them, animals that died on the road, whatever a caravan drops. They range in family groups of four to nine and hunt only what is already dying. A pack learns a funeral's route within a season and will be at the graveside before the mourners. Some cities take that as the dead being met on the road. Others take it as a warning that the rites were begun badly, and start again.

physiology.size: 45 cm at the shoulder, 1.1 m nose to tail
physiology.reproduction: A mated pair keeps to each other for life and raises one litter of four to six pups a year in a dug den. The pups run with the pack by the end of their first season, and most of a litter does not see a second one.

lore.tactics: They will not open a fight. They follow, wait for someone to fall behind, and take the smallest or the slowest. In a fight they circle rather than close. **Pack Tactics** pays only when two of them reach the same person, so run them in pairs on one target and have them give up on anyone they cannot get behind. A strong bite puts anyone of their own size or smaller prone, so send the next jackal at whoever is already down. They break off the moment it costs them anything, and one dead jackal is usually enough. They will not follow anyone who turns and advances, and they fall back to the edge of the light and wait.

table.description: Mange-thin and badly furred.
Primitive materials, Quality 1. One set of fittings.
Primitive materials, Quality 1. Twisted into cord it repairs a bowstring or binds a loose haft.
Raw meat equal to 1 x simple rations (d4) with 1 use left. At the start of each day, remove 1 use as the meat spoils.
Dragged off a graveside into the den.
A notched stick from a tomb door, chewed but readable. It matches the seal on one necropolis vault.

attacks.name: Snatching Beak
attacks.text: Roll Agility + Perception vs. Dodge. No damage. On a success, this creature takes one loose item of 0 or 1 load from the target's hands, belt, or an open container and immediately uses their Movement to fly away with it.

lore.narrative: A pigeon-sized flier, all leather wing and beaked snout, at home in harbour cities for as long as there have been harbour cities. They sit on market awnings, nest in roof beams, and take bread out of baskets nobody is watching. Sailors say a quay without leatherwings is a quay the sea has turned against, and no captain who believes it will tie up there.
lore.ecology: They eat scraps, fish guts, dropped bread, and insects. A market with leatherwings has fewer rats than a market without. Everyone who keeps records knows this. Nobody says it in a council meeting. Flocks follow the boats in and strip the guts off the water before the catch is landed. Wild colonies nest on sea cliffs. The city flocks are a separate population, and nobody brought them in. They moved into the cities as the cities grew. A trained one carries messages better than a pigeon, because a leatherwing remembers roofs and coastlines instead of a single home loft. It takes most of a year to train one, and the trainers are a small and well-paid trade.

physiology.reproduction: A pair holds one nest site for years and raises two eggs at a time, twice a year, on a cliff ledge or a roof beam. Chicks fly at ten weeks and stay with the flock they hatched in. A city colony is mostly one extended family, which is part of why they all know the same faces.

lore.tactics: Do not run them as a fight. What they do is scream. A flock that does not recognise somebody raises a racket that carries across a whole market, and while the flock is up the district is awake and watching. They remember faces, so anyone who has fed one is not a stranger to the flock for days. Use **Snatching Beak** on what is held rather than what is guarded, then go straight up to a roofline nothing can follow to. They break off by climbing out of reach, and they come back.

table.description: Tarnished, dropped in a market.
A glass bead still set in it.
Enough tackle to fish with.
Lead, half melted. Somebody sealed letters with it.
A week old, equal to 1 x simple rations (d4) with 1 use left.
Still sealed, off a courier. A clay case baked around the tablet inside. It holds one of: a shipment and a date, a name and a price, or an order nobody wants attributed.

attacks.name: Venomous Bite
attacks.text: 4/5/6 damage. On a strong or critical hit, the target is briefly poisoned.

abilities.name: Strike from Cover
abilities.text: While hidden, this creature's first attack in a scene increases the SL by one step (max. critical).

lore.narrative: A forearm-long snake the colour of dry reed. They live in the irrigation channels, and the farmers who work those channels know the sound of one leaving. They are not aggressive. They are just always lying where somebody is about to step.
lore.ecology: They hunt rats and frogs along the channel banks. They spend the heat of the day under matting, stacked reed, or in the shade of the bank. Harvest is when people meet them, because harvest is when people walk the channels barefoot. Villages do not kill them. They keep the rats down, and any that are killed are replaced within a season.

physiology.reproduction: They lay six to ten eggs under warm matting or a stacked reed pile at the end of summer and leave them there. Hatchlings are venomous from the first day and a finger's length long, which is how a village ends up with a bad stretch of channel in a single season.

lore.tactics: They strike once, from cover, at whoever puts a foot near them. **Strike from Cover** only works while they are unseen, so open from hiding and do not open twice. After the strike they leave for the water and they will not pursue. The bite is not what kills. Run the poison in somebody who is days from a healer.

table.description: Weapon Poison (weak), 1 use. Coats a weapon for 2 poison damage on a hit. Spoils within a day unless properly stored.
Primitive materials, Quality 1.
Taken whole, off a snake that shed it clean.
Raw meat equal to 1 x simple rations (d4) with 1 use left. At the start of each day, remove 1 use as the meat spoils.
Found under the same matting. An alchemist will take them.
Scratched with the sluice order for the whole valley: which gate opens when, and whose fields drink first.

attacks.name: Devouring Bites
attacks.text: 4/5/6 damage against every creature in this creature's area. On a strong or critical hit, the target is distracted until they spend an Action to brush the beetles off. While this creature is at half HP or lower, this attack deals half damage, rounded up.

lore.narrative: Finger-long scarabs that live on grave goods, funeral tallow, and the dead themselves. The priests of the necropolis call them the last of the offerings, left to eat what the living stopped bringing. Disturb the floor and they come up through it.
lore.ecology: A colony lives in the packed earth under a tomb floor. They eat the fat in funeral lamps, the leather and linen of grave goods, and anything organic left as an offering. They do not hunt. They boil up when the floor above them is walked on, worked, or broken. They do not lie in wait, so whoever wakes them has just broken the floor they nest under, and that is usually a robber, a mason, or a priest come to re-seal a chamber. A tomb with intact floors and no beetles has usually been emptied already.

physiology.reproduction: Eggs go into the packed earth in their hundreds, and the grubs feed underground for two years on whatever is buried above them. That is why a broken floor brings up a generation rather than a handful. A swarm is two to three thousand of them, and the colony they come from is as old as the tomb.

lore.tactics: They occupy an area and threaten only what stands in it, so **Devouring Bites** hits everyone who stayed. Fire drives them off and they will not cross it. A torch swept low, a lamp broken on the floor, a burning cloak dropped in a doorway, any of it turns them. They will not leave the colony's ground, and that ground is the whole chamber floor rather than one corner of it, so backing out of the room gives it up rather than winning it. Once it is empty they settle back into the floor.

table.description: Primitive materials, Quality 1, swept up by the handful.
Oil, Quality 1, 2 uses left. Rendered out of the funeral lamps.
Bronze pins, a ring, the back of a mirror.
Unbroken, with the tomb patron's seal still on the stopper. The grain inside went past eating three centuries ago.
Off a coffin face.
The tomb's plan cut into the underside. The builders left directions, and the beetles cleaned them off.

attacks.name: Grasping Hands
attacks.text: 6/9/12 damage. On a strong or critical hit, the target is grappled.

attacks.name: Bearing Down
attacks.text: 6/9/12 damage. Only against a target this creature has grappled. On a hit, the target falls prone.

abilities.name: Grave-Bound
abilities.text: This creature cannot willingly move further than a medium distance from the ground they were left on. When they are destroyed, they rise again at the next sunset unless their body is buried or burned.

lore.narrative: One of the unburied dead, walking in the body nobody said the words over. They do not remember being a person, and nothing in them wants anything. They walk a short distance from where they were left and no further. They keep doing it until somebody puts them in the ground.
lore.ecology: They do not eat, sleep, or rest, and they do not decay the way a body should. They rise where rites were skipped: plague pits, battlefields nobody came back for, robbed graves, any burial that was interrupted. They cannot be reasoned with or frightened. That, not their strength, is the practical problem. One husk on a road costs a village a week and a priest's fee. A field of them after a battle is why the temples send people.

physiology.size: Whatever the person was in life, and most of them stood 1.6 to 1.8 m
physiology.weight: 40 to 60 kg, and falling, since they dry out rather than rot
physiology.lifespan: They do not age, and a husk still walking a road may be 200 years dead

lore.tactics: They walk at whoever is closest and take hold. **Grasping Hands** grapples on a strong hit and they do not let go. Once they have hold, switch to **Bearing Down** and use it every turn after, which puts the held character prone. They never speed up, never flank and never choose a better target. They cannot follow past the ground they were left on, and **Grave-Bound** says how far that reaches. They do not rout. Killing one settles nothing, since they stand up again at the next sunset unless the body is buried or burned.

table.description: Still in the mouth. Taking passage money is not free of consequence in most cities.
Short Spear, Quality 2, damaged. Pitted through where the head meets the haft.
Thin and decorative, made for a funeral rather than for wear.
Oil, Quality 1, 3 uses. Four centuries old and it still burns.
Leather, Quality 1, broken. Rotted through at the shoulders.
The name of whoever this was. A priest needs it to lay them properly.

attacks.name: Snatch
attacks.text: Roll Agility + Stealth vs. Dodge. No damage. On a success, this creature takes one loose item of 0 or 1 load from the target's hands, belt, or an open container, and immediately uses their Movement to move away with it.

abilities.name: Quick Escape
abilities.text: When an enemy misses this creature with a melee attack, this creature moves up to a close distance unprovoked.

lore.narrative: A goblin who has learned that nobody watches the small one until it is too late, and who has never once picked a fight they were expected to win. They are not really trying to kill anybody. They are trying to leave with something, and the knife is only there in case that goes wrong.
lore.ecology: They live where a road runs past cover, which is most roads. A gang holds a stretch of it for a season, sleeps in whatever hole is nearest, and moves on when the carters start travelling armed. They eat what they take, and what they take is mostly food. Nothing about this is a war. The stretch of road matters more than the goblins on it, and a village that loses two carts in a month knows exactly which bend the trouble is at and cannot spare the men to go and look. Carters, drovers, tax collectors and pilgrims are the people who meet them, and most of the ones who do arrive late rather than not at all.

physiology.lifespan: Adult at 12, old at 35, and 50 years is a long life

lore.tactics: They do not open the fight. They wait for somebody else to, then come in from the side. **Snatch** is what they are here for, so spend their turns robbing whoever is already busy and save the knife for when somebody corners them. They take from the character with the most hanging off their belt, not the most dangerous one, and they leave with it. **Pack Tactics** wants another goblin already on the same target, so put two of them on one character rather than one each on two. Between turns they spend **Quick Escape** on the first attack that misses them. They will not stand in a line and they will not hold ground. One of them alone breaks and runs, and a gang that has lost half its number goes with it, carrying whatever it has.

table.description: Shortsword, Quality 2, damaged and fragile. Ground down from something longer.
Leather, Quality 1, damaged and fragile. Cut down from a piece made for somebody twice their size.
Coin off whoever came down this road before.
Four of them, no two a pair.
Simple Rations (d4) with 2 uses left.
A knotted cord counting the carts that have passed and the days between them. Read backward it gives the road's traffic and the place the gang watches it from.

abilities.name: Pin Them Down
abilities.text: On a strong or critical hit with their Shortbow, the target is briefly slowed.

abilities.name: Quick Escape
abilities.text: When an enemy misses this creature with a melee attack, this creature moves up to a close distance unprovoked.

lore.narrative: The one in the rocks above the road, who has been watching the track since the last bend. They shoot first, and they shoot from somewhere nobody has thought to look.
lore.ecology: They live where a road runs past cover, which is most roads. A gang holds a stretch of it for a season, sleeps in whatever hole is nearest, and moves on when the carters start travelling armed. They eat what they take, and what they take is mostly food. The bow is the one thing in a gang that gets looked after, because it is the one thing they cannot make again in an afternoon, and the goblin holding it is usually the one who has been on this road longest. Carters, drovers, tax collectors and pilgrims are the people who meet them, and most of the ones who do arrive late rather than not at all.

physiology.lifespan: Adult at 12, old at 35, and 50 years is a long life

lore.tactics: They open the fight, from cover, at whatever range the ground gives them. They shoot whoever is least protected rather than whoever is most dangerous, and they keep shooting the same one. They give up height only when they have to. In melee they are almost nothing, so **Quick Escape** goes on the first melee attack that misses them and they use it to get back to a position rather than simply away. **Pin Them Down** is the whole point of shooting low, so put it on whoever is trying to reach them and shoot that one again. The knife is a last resort. A shortage of arrows moves them off the fight faster than a wound does. They break and run alone, and they run before the skulkers do.

table.description: Shortbow, Quality 2, damaged and fragile. The upper limb is split and bound.
Shortsword, Quality 2, damaged and fragile.
Leather, Quality 1, damaged and fragile.
Primitive materials, Quality 1. Fletched with whatever was to hand, no two alike.
Silver, off a trader's neck. The house it belongs to is still trading.
A stick cut with the distance from the watch-post to each landmark along the road. Whoever holds it knows every position the gang shoots from.

abilities.name: Orcish Fury
abilities.text: When this creature hits with a melee weapon and rolls a critical success, they add their weapon damage an additional time to the total damage. The critical damage listed for their melee attacks already includes it.

abilities.name: Charge In
abilities.text: This creature gains 1 additional Movement this turn. They must use it to move closer to an enemy they can see.

lore.narrative: An orc down from the dry country at harvest, as their band has come down every harvest anyone can remember. They are not an invasion and they do not want the land. They want the grain, and they intend to be home before the season turns.
lore.ecology: Raiding bands come out of the herding country at the edge of the farmland, where nothing is sown and everything is driven. Harvest is the one season the valley is worth the ride. Twenty to forty come down together, hit the villages furthest from a garrison, and are gone inside a day. Most villages keep a standing arrangement, a portion left out and a route left unwatched, and the raids that turn violent are the ones where a new headman decided not to pay. The rest of the year these are herders, smiths and mercenaries, and the people they rob sometimes know them by name. The best known of them are the Zakhar of the canyon country, who have taken the river valley's harvest for as long as the valley has had one.

physiology.lifespan: Adult at 14, old at 45, and 60 years is a long life

lore.tactics: Javelins first, at range, while they close. **Charge In** gets them across open ground a round sooner than the party has planned for, so spend it early and arrive together rather than in ones. A raider who has already spent it has no answer to anybody leaving their reach, and that trade comes up every round. They go for whoever stands between them and the grain, not for whoever is most dangerous. **They will break off to carry away what they came for** if they can reach it. A raider who is alone and losing looks for a way out rather than a last stand.

table.description: Battleaxe, Quality 2, damaged.
Javelin, Quality 2, `bundle (d4)` with 1 use left.
Leather, Quality 1, damaged. Covers the shoulders and nothing else.
Strung on a thong, cut and polished in the holds they winter in.
Simple Rations (d4), full.
The cord a rider shows at a friendly hold to be let in and fed. Whoever carries it passes for one of the band.

attacks.name: Bite
attacks.text: 7/10/13 damage. On a strong or critical hit against a creature of equal or smaller size, the target is grappled. While grappling, this attack cannot be used against any other target.

attacks.name: Death Roll
attacks.text: Only against a target this creature has grappled. 7/10/13 damage, and the target falls prone.

lore.narrative: A river crocodile not yet at full size, small enough to lie up under a landing stage. River villages keep their children off the bank at dusk, and the fence along the bank is there for the same reason.
lore.ecology: They lie up in shallow water against a bank, a jetty, or a stand of reed, and take whatever comes down to drink. A young one hunts dogs, goats, waterfowl, and people who are alone. They avoid anything in a group. Full-grown crocodiles drive the young off the best stretches, so the ones a village meets are usually this size and usually hungry. One that has taken livestock keeps using the same crossing until something changes. The village always knows where they are.

physiology.lifespan: 60 years or more, and one this size is 4 to 6 years old
physiology.reproduction: The female buries forty eggs in the warm sand of a bank and guards the nest until they hatch. Almost none of them reach this size, and the ones that do have already been driven off the best water by something larger.

lore.tactics: They lie submerged and wait for somebody to come to the bank rather than swimming into view. Open with the **Bite** against a target who does not know they are there, since **Ambush Predator** raises that first strike one success level. The bite grapples, and the grapple is the point, because a grappled person is going into the river. They cannot hold and bite at once, so a crocodile with someone in their jaws spends the turn dragging and attacks nobody else. If the fight turns they release, submerge, and do not come back while anyone is standing on their bank.

table.description: Taken whole, then part ruined by careless skinning.
Primitive materials, Quality 1. Enough leather for one set of light armor once worked.
Primitive materials, Quality 1, a full jaw of them.
Raw meat equal to 1 x simple rations (d4) with 2 uses left. At the start of each day, remove 1 use as the meat spoils.
And what came up with them: a belt buckle, two rings, a bronze fitting.
Still on the finger. Shown at any river village it opens a headman's door, and closes every other one.

attacks.name: Pull Down
attacks.text: 6/8/10 damage. On a strong or critical hit, the target falls prone.

abilities.name: False Appearance
abilities.text: While this creature does not move, they are indistinguishable from ordinary grave goods. A creature searching the room can tell the difference with a successful Mind + Perception roll vs. TN 8.

lore.narrative: A knee-high figure of fired clay with a hoe moulded into its fists, buried by the hundred so the dead would not have to work their own fields. The potters who made them wrote the work into the clay before the firing, in an age that knew how. The potters are long gone and the figures are still working.
lore.ecology: They do not eat, wear out, or stop. The tombs of the old dynasties were buried with a chamber of them, ranked by the hundred and moulded for one task each: the diggers, the water carriers, the ones with a loom. Nobody has made one since. The work is written into a fired core, and the cutting of cores was Ghahar craft that went into the ground with the fortresses that held it, so a tomb furnished today gets painted figures that will stand in the dark forever and never lift a hoe. Ghahar smiths still raise new servants, and every one of them is built around a core dug out of somewhere older, which is most of why the old chambers get opened at all. The rule the potters worked to is still repeated by the people who set the figures out, that one moulded with its face turned from the door will not serve, so the faces all look at whoever comes in. What wakes them is the chamber being disturbed, and they go back to standing when it is quiet again.

physiology.lifespan: They do not age. A shattered figure stops and the pieces are only clay, and figures 400 years in the ground stand up when the chamber is opened

lore.tactics: They do not start a fight. **False Appearance** holds them still among the grave goods until somebody lifts something or breaks a seal, and then the whole rank moves at once. They go for the nearest hands. Use **Pull Down** to take a standing character off their feet and leave them for the next figure. They never leave the chamber they were buried in, and they mass at the doorway rather than following through it. Backing into the corridor is safe and leaves with nothing, since everything worth taking is on the floor they are standing on. They do not rout, and they stop the moment the room is quiet.

table.description: Primitive materials, Quality 2. Fine grey clay with the glaze still on it.
Tools, Quality 2. Bronze chisel and a wooden mallet, dropped by whoever came in before and never picked up again.
Coin off somebody the rank pulled down, still knotted shut.
Oil, Quality 1, 3 uses. Left for the chamber lamps.

Fired clay with the animating sigils cracked through. No smith alive can cut new ones, so an unbroken core is worth opening a tomb for. This one will never raise a servant again, and a Ghahar house will buy it anyway.
Fired into the figure's back. It names the dead this chamber was cut for and the work the figure was given. A priest can say whose tomb this is, and an heir can claim it.

attacks.name: Claws
attacks.text: 6/8/10 damage. On a strong or critical hit, the target is briefly dazed, or stunned for a short duration instead if they are already dazed. A stunned target can roll Strength + Fortitude vs. TN 8 at the end of each of their turns to end the condition early.

abilities.name: Feeding Frenzy
abilities.text: When this creature hits a stunned creature with their Bite, they regain 4 HP.

lore.narrative: A thin, quick eater of the dead, at home in the necropolis and in the graves the robbers opened first. They talk, in a fashion, and it has never once been a conversation. What they want is always the same thing, and a living person is the part of it that is still moving. The grave-wardens of the old cities know which colonies are theirs and leave a body out at the end of the season.
lore.ecology: They eat the dead and nothing else. A colony holds a stretch of burial ground and works it in pairs, going first through what has already been broken open and digging only when nothing has. After a battle they come out onto the field in numbers and there is nothing left on it by the third night, which is why several cities tolerate the colony under their necropolis and one or two feed it. They keep away from the living while there is easier food, and a bad year is when there is not. The colony is the only thing a ghoul cooperates with. Inside it they hunt in pairs, share a kill and hold a stretch of ground together, and none of that reaches anybody outside it. A city that tolerates a colony is feeding one, not dealing with one, and the wardens who work the same ground stay in twos and are careful never to be the easiest thing on it. Some hold that a ghoul is what becomes of somebody who ate the dead in a famine year. The wardens say they were never people at all, and that talking to one is talking to the hunger rather than to a person.

physiology.lifespan: They do not age, and colonies 300 years under the same necropolis are known. Hunger is what ends them, and a stretch of ground picked clean empties itself in a season

lore.tactics: They open on whoever is already hurt and they work in pairs. Lead with **Claws**, which dazes and then stuns. Against a stunned target they switch to the **Bite** and stay on it. They circle for a flank rather than pushing through a shield, and they leave a target the moment somebody easier is on the ground. They cannot be parleyed with. A torch pushed into a face turns one, and a pack that loses its nerve runs for the graves. They will not follow anyone out of the burial ground.

table.description: Primitive materials, Quality 2. A full set, still hard.
Taken whole, with the teeth in it.
Bronze pins, the back of a mirror, a string of carnelian, all off the dead they ate.
Leaf and wire, worked off a coffin face and carried home.
Oil, Quality 1, 3 uses. Out of the chamber they nest in.
The note the grave-wardens use to call a colony off a body. Ghouls that have heard it before come away, and every one within the necropolis hears it.

attacks.name: Sweeping Blow
attacks.text: This creature can only use this attack if they skip all Movement this turn, before and after the attack. 6/8/10 damage against every creature within close range.

abilities.name: Close the Ranks
abilities.text: While another creature with this ability is within melee range of this creature, attacks against this creature suffer +1 bane.

abilities.name: Over the Shields
abilities.text: While another creature with `Close the Ranks` is within melee range of this creature, this creature's attacks do not suffer the reach bane.

lore.narrative: The second rank, working over the shoulders of the shields with three metres of pole and a blade on the end of it. They are picked for reach and shoulders, and they spend the whole fight looking at the backs of their own front rank.
lore.ecology: They are paid at the start of the season and drilled for the rest of it. A file stands watches, walks the wall, escorts carts and grain barges, and fights perhaps twice a year. Most were taken on at sixteen for the food and the coin, and most go home at thirty with a bad shoulder and a plot of land they were promised. They eat better than the people they guard and they know it. Off duty they are in the same wineshops as everybody else. A file that has stood together for a season is closer than most families, and the older soldiers hold that a line which loses its right-hand man twice will not stand a third time, so a file that loses two is broken up and shared out.

physiology.note: Depends on the folk of this creature. See "Physical Traits by Folk" in the Folk section for more details.

lore.tactics: They stand behind a shield and hit what the shield is holding. **Over the Shields** only works while somebody is in front of them, so keep them in the second rank and move them along the line rather than out of it. They drag people out of cover and off the flanks toward the spears. **Sweeping Blow** costs them their movement for the turn, so save it for the moment the party bunches up. They hold as long as the shields do and break with them.

table.description: Glaive, Quality 2, damaged. The haft is cracked below the head.
Leather, Quality 1, damaged.
Oil, Quality 1, 2 uses left. Carried for the blade.
Coin drawn at the muster, in a purse sewn inside the cuirass.
Simple Rations (d4) with 1 use left.
An incised tablet of what the file is owed. Three of the names on it draw wages and do not stand in the line, and the officer who wrote it knows.

abilities.name: Close the Ranks
abilities.text: While another creature with this ability is within melee range of this creature, attacks against this creature suffer +1 bane.

abilities.name: Ranging Shot
abilities.text: On a strong or critical hit with a ranged weapon, the target suffers marked (2).

lore.narrative: The one behind the shields with a bag of cast lead, who has been told which target and does not have to think about the rest. They are the cheapest soldier a city fields and the one their own line stands in front of.
lore.ecology: They are paid at the start of the season and drilled for the rest of it. A file stands watches, walks the wall, escorts carts and grain barges, and fights perhaps twice a year. Most were taken on at sixteen for the food and the coin, and most go home at thirty with a bad shoulder and a plot of land they were promised. They eat better than the people they guard and they know it. Off duty they are in the same wineshops as everybody else. A file that has stood together for a season is closer than most families, and the older soldiers hold that a line which loses its right-hand man twice will not stand a third time, so a file that loses two is broken up and shared out.

physiology.note: Depends on the folk of this creature. See "Physical Traits by Folk" in the Folk section for more details.

lore.tactics: They stay behind the shields and shoot over them. Put **Ranging Shot** on whoever the line is about to reach rather than on whoever is nearest, and shoot the same target twice before choosing another. They fall back the moment somebody gets past the shields, and draw the shortsword only when cornered. With the line gone they break and run.

table.description: Sling, Quality 2, damaged. The cradle is cut through.
Shortsword, Quality 2, damaged.
Leather, Quality 1, damaged.
Primitive materials, Quality 2. Thirty of them in a bag, all of one weight.
Coin drawn at the muster, and less of it than the shield ranks draw.
A cord the file knots as they march, one knot to the landmark and one to the day. Run backward it is the road to the camp they came from.

attacks.name: Shield Bash
attacks.text: 6/8/10 damage. On a strong or critical hit, the target falls prone.

abilities.name: Close the Ranks
abilities.text: While another creature with this ability is within melee range of this creature, attacks against this creature suffer +1 bane.

abilities.name: Braced Spear
abilities.text: When using Opportunity Attack with their Spear, this creature deals +2 damage and the target's Movement ends.

lore.narrative: A trained soldier of a city or a warlord, three years drilled, standing behind a painted shield with the spear held level. They have never fought anything that was not standing in a line opposite them. They are very good at the one thing they do.
lore.ecology: They are paid at the start of the season and drilled for the rest of it. A file stands watches, walks the wall, escorts carts and grain barges, and fights perhaps twice a year. Most were taken on at sixteen for the food and the coin, and most go home at thirty with a bad shoulder and a plot of land they were promised. They eat better than the people they guard and they know it. Off duty they are in the same wineshops as everybody else. A file that has stood together for a season is closer than most families, and the older soldiers hold that a line which loses its right-hand man twice will not stand a third time, so a file that loses two is broken up and shared out.

physiology.note: Depends on the folk of this creature. See "Physical Traits by Folk" in the Folk section for more details.

lore.tactics: They form up and hold. They will not chase individuals and will not spread out, but the line advances as a line and walks down anyone shooting at it. They give ground a step at a time rather than open it. Keep them shoulder to shoulder, since **Close the Ranks** pays only while they have a neighbour, and close the gap whenever one goes down. They attack whoever comes at the line rather than whoever is most dangerous. **Braced Spear** catches anyone trying to leave their reach, so hold the position and let people walk into it. They fight until their file breaks, then run with it.

table.description: Spear, Quality 2, damaged. Split through the socket.
Light Shield, Quality 2, damaged. Faced with the mark of whoever pays them.
Leather, Quality 1, damaged.
Coin drawn at the muster, carried in a neck pouch.
Simple Rations (d4) with 2 uses left.

A clay tag with the garrison officer's seal rolled into it, carried by whoever is sent out on an errand. The gate guards know the seal and do not know the faces, so it opens the city gate for whoever holds it.

abilities.name: Orcish Fury
abilities.text: When this creature hits with a melee weapon and rolls a critical success, they add their weapon damage an additional time to the total damage. The critical damage listed for their melee attacks already includes it.

abilities.name: Fight Where I Point
abilities.text: One ally within short range gains +1 boon on their next attack, and on a hit the target is briefly slowed.

abilities.name: Batter Aside
abilities.text: When an enemy within melee range attacks this creature, that attack suffers +1 bane. If the attack fails, this creature makes one Maul attack against them.

abilities.name: Blood Up
abilities.text: When this creature suffers a Wound, the rage takes them and they stop caring whether they live. For the rest of the scene their melee attacks gain +1 boon and deal +2 damage, and melee attacks against them gain +1 boon.

lore.narrative: The one who chose the village, and the one who will decide when it is finished. They have ridden this country for twenty years and have never once fought to the last orc. That is why they are still the one choosing.
lore.ecology: A band-leader holds the band by being right about what a raid is worth, not by being the strongest in it. They know which villages pay, which have a garrison within a day, and which headman will talk. Most have a name in the country they ride. Some have an understanding with the people they take from, renewed every harvest and kept on both sides more often than either would admit. A band that loses their leader does not usually pick another that season. They go home.

physiology.lifespan: Adult at 14, old at 45, and 60 years is a long life

lore.tactics: They stay behind the line and run it rather than fighting in it. Spend **Fight Where I Point** on whichever raider is best placed, and hold the Quick Action for **Batter Aside** when somebody finally reaches them, because they cannot do both in one round. The maul is for whoever is armored and the javelin for whoever is not close enough yet. Once they are Wounded, **Blood Up** puts them in the front rank trading hits and they stop directing anybody. **They can be bought at any point before that.** Offer them the grain and they take it and go.

table.description: Maul, Quality 3, damaged. Bronze head over a hardwood core, wound with silver wire.
Banded Leather, Quality 2, damaged. The source of their AV.
River-city seals, none of them theirs, taken over three seasons. Two of the owners are still alive.
Worn as a record of raids. Taking them off a living leader is an insult.
12 x Simple Rations (d4). Where the band was going next.
Incised clay with two marks, a village and a band. It proves the raids were arranged.

abilities.name: Quick Escape
abilities.text: When an enemy misses this creature with a melee attack, this creature moves up to a close distance unprovoked.

abilities.name: Get In Front
abilities.text: When an enemy attacks this creature while an ally is within melee range of this creature, that attack targets that ally instead.

abilities.name: Spring the Trap
abilities.text: When this creature suffers a Wound, they whistle, and the goblins who were waiting for the signal come down. Two Goblin Skulkers arrive within short range of this creature, from cover or higher ground if there is any. Every ally within short range of this creature immediately moves up to a short distance unprovoked.

lore.narrative: The one who chose this bend in the road, told everyone where to stand, and has already decided which way they personally are leaving. They hold the gang by being right about which carts are worth stopping.
lore.ecology: A ringleader holds a gang by judgement rather than by strength, and most of them are the smallest thing in it. They know which stretch of road is watched, which villages will pay to be left alone, and which drover will hand over half a load rather than lose a wheel. Some of those arrangements run for years and are renewed every season. A gang that loses their ringleader scatters within the week and turns up on somebody else's road. The ones who last are the ones who never let a robbery become a fight.

physiology.lifespan: Adult at 12, old at 35, and 50 years is a long life

lore.tactics: They start the fight and then get out of it, running the gang from the back with the lash reaching over the top of them. **Get In Front** puts whoever is beside them in the way of anything aimed at them, so keep a skulker within arm's reach at all times and treat the gang as their armor. The lash is for anyone unarmored and the javelins for anyone who is not, and they will spend a whole fight at range if the ground allows. They compete for one Quick Action between **Get In Front** and **Quick Escape**, so once the goblins beside them are down the escape is all they have left. Once they are Wounded, **Spring the Trap** brings two more goblins down off the rocks and shifts everyone already fighting into a better position, so fire it before the gang is spent rather than after. **They can be bought before that and not after.** Take the toll and they wave the party through, and the deal holds only as long as the party keeps travelling that road.

table.description: Whip, Quality 2, damaged and fragile. Bone beads worked into the last hand of it.
Javelin, Quality 2, damaged and fragile. `bundle (d4)` with 2 uses left.
Coins from six polities, pierced and strung in the order they were taken.
Five of them, off five travellers. Two of the owners are alive and looking.
8 x Simple Rations (d4), off a load that was going somewhere else.
A hide scratched with this road, every place the gang watches it from, and the three villages that pay them not to come down. Two of those villages would rather it was not found.

attacks.name: Shield Bash
attacks.text: 6/8/10 damage. On a strong or critical hit, the target falls prone.

abilities.name: Close the Ranks
abilities.text: While another creature with this ability is within melee range of this creature, attacks against this creature suffer +1 bane.

abilities.name: Step Into the Gap
abilities.text: When an enemy attacks an ally within short range of this creature, this creature moves into melee range of that ally and makes one attack against the attacker.

abilities.name: Nothing New
abilities.text: This creature briefly ignores the effects of the frightened condition.

lore.narrative: A soldier past forty, taken on at sixteen and still standing in the line at an age when most of the file has gone home to a plot of land. They carry the same spear and the same painted shield as the soldier beside them, and every strap on the kit has been replaced twice. The officers put them where the line is expected to break.
lore.ecology: They draw the same pay as everybody else in the file and are worth three of them. A veteran is not given a rank and does not ask for one, because a rank means standing behind the line and giving orders instead of holding a place in it. Officers move them from file to file along the wall, and a file that has been given one knows it has been marked as the weak one. Off duty they drink with the young soldiers and tell them nothing useful. Most of them have a plot of land waiting somewhere they have stopped meaning to go to, and the older soldiers hold that somebody who has stood twenty years in a line will not know what to do with a field.

physiology.note: Depends on the folk of this creature. See "Physical Traits by Folk" in the Folk section for more details.

lore.tactics: They take the worst place in the line and stay in it. Keep them shoulder to shoulder, since **Close the Ranks** pays only while somebody is beside them. They fight at reach with the **Spear** and hold their one Quick Action for **Step Into the Gap**, which carries them to a threatened neighbour and answers the attacker, or spend it on **Nothing New** when fear is the bigger problem. They attack whoever is on their neighbour rather than whoever is most dangerous, and they are the last of the file to run.

table.description: Spear, Quality 2, damaged. Bound at the socket with wire, twice over.
Light Shield, Quality 2, damaged. Faced over twice, and the marks underneath belong to two different cities.
Banded Leather, Quality 2, damaged. Cut and restitched to fit somebody wider than it was made for.
Their share of a town that was taken, carried on the body because they do not trust a strongbox.
Simple Rations (d4) with 2 uses left.
A short bronze horn on a cord. Two notes bring the nearest patrol to the sound, and every soldier of that city has been drilled to come. It does not ask who blew it.

attacks.name: Fist
attacks.text: 8/11/14 damage. On a strong or critical hit against a creature of Medium size or smaller, the target is grappled.

abilities.name: Hurl
abilities.text: Only against a creature this creature is grappling. This creature throws the target a short distance in any direction, resolved as if the target were pushed that distance. Roll Strength + Athletics vs. Dodge against each creature in the space the target is thrown into. On a success, the target collides with them, and both take the damage and fall prone. On a failure, that creature gets clear. As an Action instead of a Quick Action, this creature can throw a Small or Medium object within their reach the same way, and only the creature struck takes the damage.

lore.narrative: Three metres tall and always hungry, with a tree for a club and a shoulder like a wall. Ogres are the smallest of the giants and the only ones that live where people do, out on the bad ground that no city has ever bothered to claim. They will take a price and stand guard for a season, which has convinced a great many people that an ogre is somebody you can come to an arrangement with. The arrangement lasts exactly as long as the ogre is fed.
lore.ecology: They eat constantly and they are not particular. An ogre works a stretch of hill or marsh the way a bear does, walking the same round every few days, taking whatever is slow, and coming down onto the farmland when the round runs thin. They know that people carry food and they have learned that people are food. Ogres are the only giants that deal with anyone. They keep to twos and threes, they know enough trade-speech to name a price, and a village will pay them in cattle to be left alone while a raiding band hires one for a season. None of that makes them a people. An ogre keeps no custom and remembers no agreement past the day it fed them, so a bargain holds while it is the easiest food in reach and breaks the hour it is not, without warning. Everybody who deals with an ogre knows this and does it anyway, because the alternative is having the ogre come to them. The priests say the giants came out of the titans and have never forgiven the world for what came after. An ogre asked about it says nothing that settles the question.

physiology.lifespan: Adult at 20, and 200 years is an ordinary age for one
physiology.reproduction: One child at a time after a long carrying, perhaps three in a life, and the young stay with the mother until they can bring down something on their own.

lore.tactics: They walk straight in and open with the **Great Club** before anyone gets close. Once somebody is right up against them the club is no use, so they switch to the **Fist**, and a grabbed character goes into the nearest group with **Hurl** on the same turn. Against a party that stays back they throw whatever is lying around instead. They go for the smallest person they can lift, and break off once they have something worth carrying. Livestock buys off this fight and nothing later, so an ogre the party has paid turns on them the moment something easier stands closer.

table.description: Crafting material, Quality 3. Long bones, dense enough to work into hafts and roof beams.
The lower pair, taken out whole. A bounty officer knows them on sight.
1 x simple rations (d4) with 2 uses left. At the start of each day, remove 1 use as the meat spoils.
Buckles, rings and a bent bracelet, sorted into a fold of hide because the ogre likes the noise.
Battleaxe, Quality 2, damaged. Off somebody who came for the bounty and did not manage it.

A goat hide with the herding routes cut into it and the wells marked along each one. It is the safe way through the hills. One stretch has been crossed out twice, and that stretch is where this ogre works.

abilities.name: Spellcasting
abilities.text: This creature can cast the following spells, rolling Spirit + Mysticism: *Cloud of Sickness*, *Curse of Death*, *Rotting Grasp*. This creature can cast each of these spells once per scene.

abilities.name: Grave-Smoke
abilities.text: On a strong or critical hit with their Censer, this creature swings the chain so the smoke breaks across the target's face. The target is briefly blinded.

lore.narrative: A priest of a fringe death-cult, keeping rites the orthodox temples struck off their calendars. They meet at night in a necropolis nobody has swept in years, in a robe that smells of the censer, with a mark of their cult cut into everything they own. What they offer the people who come down to them is that death is a power worth speaking to, and that they know how to speak to it.
lore.ecology: They are not a temple and they do not have one. A cult like this is nine or ten people who meet in a crypt on the nights the calendar says nothing happens, and the priest is whoever learned the words from the last one. They sit with the dying the temples will not sit with, and they lay out the dead of families who cannot pay for a proper burial, and they do the work for nothing. That is most of how they grow. The orthodox priesthoods call the rites heresy and the city watches call them a nuisance, and neither of them goes into the necropolis after dark to do anything about it. Where a colony of ghouls holds ground the cult wants, the cult feeds them exactly as the grave-wardens do and tells itself the prayer is the difference. Some say it is one of their rites that leaves a body walking instead of resting. The cult says those are the rites somebody interrupted.

physiology.note: Depends on the folk of this creature. See "Physical Traits by Folk" in the Folk section for more details.

lore.tactics: They open with **Spellcasting** and spend all three spells in the first three rounds rather than holding any back. *Cloud of Sickness* goes on the tightest group, *Curse of Death* on whoever is hardest to kill, and *Rotting Grasp* on anyone who reaches them. After that they swing the **Censer** so **Grave-Smoke** can blind whoever is on them. They keep something between themselves and the party and give ground. They can be talked to before the rite starts and not once it has, and a spent priest runs for the crypt.

table.description: Flail, which the catalogue counts as a Mace, Quality 2, damaged. Pierced bronze bowl on a chain, still warm.
Spell Catalyst (Mystic Talisman), Quality 2. A bronze snake swallowing its own tail, worn against the skin.
Banded Leather, Quality 2, damaged. Worn under the robe and not meant to be seen.
Pins, a string of carnelian and a gold mouth-plate, all given by families who had nothing else to give.
Oil, Quality 1, 3 uses. Burns in the censer and in the chamber lamps.
A clay cylinder cut with the rite-name the cult uses for what they serve. An orthodox priest who reads it can close the shrine it was cut for. They will want to know where it was found first.

attacks.name: Shield Bash
attacks.text: 7/10/13 damage. On a strong or critical hit, the target is pushed close and this creature moves into melee range of them.

abilities.name: Close the Ranks
abilities.text: While another creature with this ability is within melee range of this creature, attacks against this creature suffer +1 bane.

abilities.name: Dress the Line
abilities.text: When an enemy attacks an ally within short range of this creature, that attack suffers +1 bane. If the attack fails, that ally immediately moves up to a close distance toward this creature unprovoked.

abilities.name: Set the Shield
abilities.text: This creature gains +2 Parry and cannot use Movement until the start of their next turn.

abilities.name: Hold the Line
abilities.text: When this creature suffers a Wound, the file closes up and stops giving ground. For the rest of the scene, every ally within short range of this creature gains +1 boon on their attacks, and this creature can use one Action to attack with both their Longsword and their Shield Bash, each against a different target.

lore.narrative: An officer of a city or a warlord, appointed out of a landholding family and handed a company to keep alive. They wear the same leather as their soldiers and carry a sword instead of a spear, which is how everyone on the field knows which one they are. They have never had to fight in the front rank.
lore.ecology: A captain is appointed rather than promoted, usually out of a family that holds land near the city and can be held to account if the company goes wrong. They draw ten times a soldier's pay, eat better than their soldiers, and are expected to spend some of the difference on them. Most of the work is not fighting. They count the muster, sign for the grain, walk the wall at night, and settle whatever their soldiers have done in the wineshops. Both sides know an officer is worth more alive than dead, so a captain taken in the field is held for ransom and the letters go back and forth for a season. Their own soldiers know it too, and a file that believes its captain would sell them does not stand.

physiology.note: Depends on the folk of this creature. See "Physical Traits by Folk" in the Folk section for more details.

lore.tactics: They fight from inside their own file rather than in front of it. Their one Quick Action goes to **Dress the Line** for an ally under attack and to **Set the Shield** when the attention turns on them. They take whoever has broken into the formation with the **Longsword**, and use **Shield Bash** to push someone off an ally and follow them. After **Hold the Line** they look for two enemies in reach at once. They do not chase and they do not rout, and cornered with the file gone they offer a ransom.

table.description: Longsword, Quality 3, damaged. Given at the appointment, with the giver's mark under the grip.
Light Shield, Quality 3, damaged. Faced in beaten bronze rather than painted hide.
Banded Leather, Quality 2, damaged. Deliberately plain, so the sword is the only thing that marks them.
Silver, worn on the chest. Seals the company's letters and draws its grain ration.
Luxury Rations (d8) with 2 uses left.

An incised tablet under a clay seal, naming who bought this company, what they were sent to do, and the sum. The city that sent them will pay to have it back, and the city they were sent against will pay more.
